title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC0RE_1LA1LD_0LB1LF_1RC1RA_1LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC0RE_1LA1LD_0LB1LF_1RC1RA_1LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of blocks. On the way right the head rewrites them as copies of 10, and on the way left it turns them back into ones. Each time the head reaches the left end, block i has lost about 2i+2 ones: the list counts like the digits of a binary counter, refilling blocks that run low. Lean proves the three shift rules of the sweeps. The list map, with its refills, has not been worked out.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 81,751 cells have been visited and 45,246 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: f_left: going left, each 1010 becomes 1111 (8 steps a word). e_right: going right, each 1111 becomes 1010 again (4 steps a word). a_right: A turns a block of 2n ones into (01)^n. All three hold for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: Lists at the left end
claims.text: At the left end the tape is 1^x0 0 1^x1 0 ... 0 1^xr. At steps 69,844,480 and 267,430,903 the lists are [110,366,822,558,166,834,330,1562,...] and [110,358,806,526,102,706,74,1050,...]. The differences are 0, −8, −16, −32, −64, −128, ... until a block runs low and is refilled. No halt in 4·109 steps.

claims.title: The law between refills
claims.text: Between visits to the left end where no block runs out and the list does not start with a lone 1, block i (i ≥ 1) loses exactly 2<sup>i+2</sup> ones and a new last block appears, e.g. [145,118,6,70,118,374] after [146,126,22,102,182] (differences −1, −8, −16, −32, −64). This was checked on 4 such pairs up to 1.5·10<sup>10</sup> steps; the other pairs involve refills or a leading block of length 1.

claims.title: A binary counter with refills
claims.text: The halving and doubling between ones and copies of 10 make the blocks lose amounts in powers of 2, like the digits of a binary counter counting down. When a block runs low, it is refilled by an amount that depends on its neighbours. This refill is the irregular step.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts if F reads a 1.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine walks back and forth over a row of blocks. Each pass rewrites them, ones into copies of 10 and back, and the blocks shrink by 4, 8, 16, 32, ... cells from one visit of the left end to the next. That is a binary counter written in block lengths.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 81,751 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Ones on the way left, copies of 10 on the way right
html: At the left end the tape is 1^x0 0 1^x1 0 ... 0 1^xr: blocks of ones separated by single 0s. On the way right, A and E rewrite each block as copies of 10. On the way left, F turns 1010 into 1111 again. These three shift rules are proved in Lean. Between the two directions, the block lengths change by small amounts, and these changes add up to the counter.
From the second row to the third, the blocks after the first lose 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 and 512. Machine 1RB0RE_1LC1LF_1RA1LD_0LB---_1RF1LE_0LB0RA does the same in base 4.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.477).
After 109 steps the tape spans 81,751 cells (59 left of the start, 60,779 right), with a density of 1s of 0.553.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RC_1LC1LE_1RD0RA_1LB0RA_0LD1LF_1LD---: rename A→C, B→D, C→B, D→E, E→A, F→F; it is this table started in state E
  • 1RB0LD_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_1LB1LC_0RA1RF_1RA---: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→E, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB1RE_1LC0LD_1RA0LD_1LA1LB_0RC1RF_1RC---: rename A→B, B→C, C→A, D→E, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: A list of blocks of ones that are rewritten as copies of 10 and back on each sweep; between visits to the left end block i shrinks by about 2^(i+2), a base-2 counter on block lengths with irregular refills.
family: base-2 counter on block lengths (block list)
